subject.title: feat: centralized filename encoding utility for multi-encoding Content-Disposition handling

question: Where should the shared multi-encoding filename decoder live, and should the existing candidate PR be refreshed or replaced?
rationale: The code gap is clear, but the permanent boundary affects core media, bundled channel plugins, and plugin-facing reuse; automation should not choose that API direction without maintainer intent.

options.title: Use a media-core/plugin-safe decoder
options.body: Move the decoder into media-core or an explicitly exported plugin-safe SDK boundary, then refresh the candidate PR or a replacement around that one shared helper.

options.title: Keep narrow channel repairs only
options.body: Treat the current Feishu fixes as sufficient for now and defer non-Feishu multi-encoding cases until concrete channel reports arrive.

options.title: Pause for broader live repros
options.body: Keep this issue open but require real non-Feishu channel failures before approving a shared utility.

recommendation.title: Use a media-core/plugin-safe decoder
recommendation.body: Move the decoder into media-core or an explicitly exported plugin-safe SDK boundary, then refresh the candidate PR or a replacement around that one shared helper.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged Feishu filename recovery and release/media-core context make this the strongest available owner for the API-boundary choice.
